The Medicaid Long-Term Planning Checklist

What to keep organized, notice and ask about when you're planning ahead for Dad.

Download PDF

Dad is managing on his own, and Medicaid is a “someday, maybe” in your family. You don't need to know any rules to use this list: it names the records worth keeping organized, the everyday changes worth noticing, and the questions worth writing down for later. Go through it with Dad's say-so and check what you've done. Anything unchecked is something to get to when it suits you both, not a verdict about Dad or about you.

Keep organized

Notice

Ask about

What this checklist doesn't do

It helps you keep, notice and ask. It doesn't say what Medicaid requires after an approval in Dad's state, whether any change on your list matters or would have to be reported, or whether Dad will ever need Medicaid. Rules vary by state, so those questions go to your Medicaid planner or the appropriate licensed professional. Nothing here is legal, financial or tax advice.

Where this comes from

Items marked 1 follow the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau's advice on keeping financial documents and professional contacts organized and letting someone you trust know where to find them. The rest come from the Medicaid Planning Roadmap's own working list for this step.
